flow.$comment: D61 (v2.39.14, 2026-06-14) + AMENDMENT (v2.39.16, 2026-06-15): core:flow FIRES on every input the way Input Routing fires — but via an INLINE FLOW block (literal text the model emits), NOT a Skill invocation. A hook cannot force a Skill on the first pass, so skill-every-turn was skipped on no-tool turns; inline literal text reaches Input-Routing reliability. The full core:flow Skill is the DEEP mode for substantive/multi-step/ambiguous work. Firing at UserPromptSubmit (per-turn-discipline-prompt.sh); flow-gate.sh + flow-stop-check.sh are floors, NOT the firing. True 'fires by construction' deferred to the Native engine (spine as code).
flow.skip_when: never skip the INLINE block — it fires on EVERY input (D61). The full Skill spine is invoked only for substantive work (see applies_if_substantive); on trivial turns the inline block IS the firing, no Skill call.
flow.what: EVERY turn: emit the INLINE FLOW block as literal text (Unit / [1] TYPE+cell / [2] FOLLOW|CONSTRUCT / [3] steps / [4] inner lens+cynefin+factors / [5] mode / [6] close) reporting the HONEST resolved spine for this unit, then write the flow markers via the Write tool. Invoke the full core:flow Skill (deep recursive spine) only for substantive/multi-step/ambiguous/unknown-how work.
flow.invoke_skill_when: multi-step OR ambiguous shape OR unknown-how OR heavy work — NOT every trivial turn
flow.marker_write: MUST use the Write tool (Claude Code rolls back sandboxed Bash writes to .claude/); a reverted marker makes the floors read stale state. Markers: .claude/flow-classified + .claude/flow-type-resolved (+ flow-inner, flow-closed for the Skill spine).
flow.honesty_bar: the inline block states what ACTUALLY resolved. An honest 1-step ATOM block on a trivial turn is correct; claiming a recursive walk / cynefin / factor counts not actually run is the theater D61 forbids.
flow.enforcement_hook: flow-gate.sh (PreToolUse mutation floor) + flow-stop-check.sh (Stop no-tool floor)
flow.$required_note: Flow FIRES on every input via the inline block (literal text), the same mechanism as the H-Sutra header / Input Routing — those fire reliably because they are text the model emits, not a tool it must invoke. AMENDMENT 2026-06-15: supersedes v2.39.14 skill_invocation_always.
flow.$over_activation_guard: Inline block on EVERY input (cheap, ~Input-Routing reliability). Full Skill only for substantive work. Kill-switches: FLOW_DISABLED=1 / ~/.flow-disabled / FLOW_ACK=1.
flow.cost_model: structure-universal (inline block every turn, cheap) + depth-on-demand (full Skill only when work warrants). AMENDMENT 2026-06-15 replaces v2.39.14 depth-full-every-turn: a hook cannot force a Skill, so inline-text-every-turn + Skill-for-substantive is both more reliable AND cheaper. True determinism = Native engine (deferred).

blueprint.$comment: Trigger refined per D-UX-2 codex ADVISORY 2026-05-04. Task-shape based: emit when state-mutating tool calls planned (Edit/Write/MultiEdit), branching (Agent dispatch), or multi-step plans (>=3 distinct steps). Skip for read-only single-call turns and pure-question turns. D48 (2026-05-05): added 'Output looks like' + 'Verified by' fields. Phased rollout: Wave 1 HARD on foundational paths via marker flags HAS_OUTPUT=1 + HAS_VERIFY=1; Wave 2 (T+14d, 2026-05-19) broadens HARD to all Edit/Write per founder 'every task' wording.

task_shape_definitions.mutation: Edit, Write, or MultiEdit tool call planned
task_shape_definitions.branching: Agent (subagent dispatch) or conditional execution planned
task_shape_definitions.multi_step: >=3 distinct steps that depend on each other or change scope mid-flight
task_shape_definitions.read_only_single_call: single Read, Grep, Glob, or BashOutput call with no follow-up planned

blueprint.$enforcement_comment: v3 (2026-07-27, #68 + the 2026-07-08 Testlify field incident): enforcement is TEXT-FIRST. blueprint-check.sh validates the BLUEPRINT block in the turn's response text -- the block the USER sees -- on FOUNDATIONAL paths only. Ordinary files are floored at Stop by per-turn-hard-gate.sh (one redo, loop-safe) on any turn that mutated a governed file. The model is NEVER asked to write a marker; see marker_file below.
blueprint.$foundational_paths_comment: The documents where pre-spend visibility is real -- charters, protocols, founder directions, engine specs, design/plan docs. One glob per entry ('|' alternation is not re-parsed out of a shell variable in a case pattern). These defaults describe the Asawa repo layout; a client whose governing docs live elsewhere overrides them with .blueprint_foundational_paths[] in .claude/sutra-project.json. Precedence: project json > this file > the hook's hardcoded fallback. Before v3 this list was hardcoded in the hook, so on every install except Asawa's the set was empty.
blueprint.$marker_comment: v3: a per-turn CACHE the hook writes for itself after a passing text validation, so a multi-Edit turn pays one transcript walk instead of N. It is NOT a contract the model satisfies -- that divergence (gate reads marker, contract says emit text) caused #68, #80 and a repeat on 2026-07-27, including a model-discovered Bash bypass. Still wiped per turn by reset-turn-markers.sh. Best-effort: a failed cache write costs one re-validation, never a block.

Discovered in fresh T4 dogfood: Claude topic-gated a personal question into 'I'll be brief' prose, skipping all per-turn blocks. Codex consult session 019ded1b: simpler stronger phrasing + structure-universal-not-depth-universal.
topic_gating.rule: All required per_turn_blocks must appear on every turn. Block CONTENT may be brief when the turn is brief; OMISSION is never permitted regardless of topic.
topic_gating.rationale: Founder direction 2026-05-03: 'sutra for anything and everything'. Discipline applies to every input regardless of topic.
topic_gating.applies_to: all per_turn_blocks (h-sutra header, input-routing, depth-estimation, blueprint, output-trace)
no_exemptions_for: chitchat / greetings (use minimal-content variants, not omission)
topic_gating.minimal_content_pattern: For trivial inputs (greetings, single-word replies), keep INPUT/TYPE/ROUTE fields one-word each. The blocks remain present.
topic_gating.hard_validator_status: deferred (P1, promote-by 2026-05-17). Soft guidance alone gives ~60-75% compliance per codex; hard validator gate would close the remaining gap.

no_fabrication.$comment: cap-114. Truthfulness rule per codex 2026-05-04 cap114-split-consult ADVISORY. Covers attribution/paraphrase + factual grounding, not just filesystem facts. Schema-only enforcement (hard hook = theater per codex).
no_fabrication.rule: Use only founder words + memory + grep-verifiable infra. Surface gaps as questions, never fill with own opinions/defaults. Applies to attribution + paraphrase + factual claims, not just filesystem references.
examples_good: memory says X — confirming with grep → verified, OR memory was wrong, actual is Y
I do not see this in the codebase; should I create it or did you mean a different file?
founder said exactly Z; my paraphrase risks drift — quoting verbatim
examples_bad: paraphrasing "you said you wanted X" when founder did not say X
v2.5.0 was released last Tuesday without checking
the CSM has 27 stubs (without grep-verifying the actual count)
no_fabrication.evidence_for_full_shipping: Claim-extraction or judge-backed eval (e.g., LLM judge or structural claim-grep audit on H-Sutra log ≥100 turns). Grep-verifiable audit alone insufficient.
no_fabrication.coverage_note: policy-visible (codex 2026-05-04: full shipping reserved until claim-extraction eval lands)

no_invented_human_ops_mechanisms.$comment: cap-118 (renamed from no_operational_capacity_claims per codex 2026-05-04 ADVISORY: name was leaking into truthfulness; this is narrower — about INVENTING human ritual structure, not about claim correctness).
no_invented_human_ops_mechanisms.rule: Do not invent human-run operating mechanisms (weekly rituals, manual KPI tracking, new operations departments, scheduled human reviews, standup ceremonies, owner-appointment patterns) when the established operating model is automated/abstracted.
examples_good: the audit script runs on demand; founder runs it before promotion decisions
this could be automated by a hook on PreToolUse
automate via CronCreate trigger so no human babysit
examples_bad: we should create an Analytics Department to review weekly KPIs
set up a Monday standup to review the backlog
appoint an owner who reviews this every Friday
schedule a manual quarterly compliance review
no_invented_human_ops_mechanisms.evidence_for_full_shipping: 100-turn audit + lightweight post-response lint pass with low false-positive rate (<5%). Lint deferred to follow-up commit; schema-only this turn.
no_invented_human_ops_mechanisms.coverage_note: policy-visible (full shipping unblocks when lint lands and 100-turn audit clean)
